Joint mode genuinely evaluates candidate pairs rather than greedily selecting the best first origin. The surface sampler is deterministic and correctly samples triangles in proportion to world-space area using barycentric coordinates. Origin evaluation includes actual segment occlusion, geometric face normals, viewing angle, approximate projected texel density, separate visibility and usable-coverage bitsets, and continuous quality values. The joint-pair mode checks every legal coarse pair, ranks them by bitset union, and only then applies quality and contribution tie-breakers. The shared coarse-to-fine engine uses 4,096 coarse samples, 256 candidates, retained pair seeds, 24,576 fine samples, local offsets, and separate fixed-first and joint branches. Tests cover deterministic sampling, double-sided occlusion, marginal second-origin ranking, non-greedy pair ranking, candidate generation, and both search modes. However, the implementation is not production-ready for complex imported sets (readiness rated 4/10). Six blockers were identified: (1) Imported sets can produce zero legal candidates because the extractor stores the entire object's AABB as an obstacle, rejecting any origin inside it; fix requires actual geometry clearance via point-to-triangle distance or shapecast, with obstacle bounds per connected mesh or spatial cluster. (2) Geometry representation will not scale to heavy imports—every triangle is expanded to JavaScript objects with three Vec3 arrays, normals, IDs, and area; for 3 million triangles this requires ~144 MB minimum packed, but actual representation is several times larger and structured-cloned into the worker, creating enormous temporary representations; BVH recursively sorts JavaScript index arrays, and every triangle intersection allocates temporary three-element arrays causing extreme GC pressure; fix requires compact typed arrays (Float32Array positions, Uint32Array indices, optional normals, meshRanges, transforms), transferring ArrayBuffers instead of cloning nested objects, and using three-mesh-bvh or a flat typed-array BVH with in-place partitioning. (3) Geometry extraction still blocks the main thread—the panel synchronously calls extractCoverageScene before creating/posting to the worker, so scene recreation, triangle flattening, world-transform application, geometry disposal, and structured cloning all happen on the main thread; extraction needs to move into the worker or become chunked with yields between meshes. (4) 'Apply to selected panorama pair' is conceptually wrong—the UI allows optimized origins to be written directly into existing panorama references via updatePanoReference, but changing metadata does not transform the image; correct workflow preserves existing panoramas, moves capture origins, renders new graybox panoramas, inpaints/generates styled panoramas, imports them as secondary panoramas, and associates each imported result with its actual origin. (5) The reachable upper bound is mathematically inconsistent—reachableCoverage uses coarse sample bank and all coarse candidates, while final combined coverage uses a different fine sample bank generated with seed+1, so UI can show Combined coverage: 83%, Reachable upper bound: 80%, Reachable captured: 100%; additionally, for fixed-first the reachable set is calculated before the arbitrary first origin is evaluated, so the fixed first origin is not included in the reachable upper bound at all; fix requires a common validation sample bank for final pair coverage, reachable candidate union, and efficiency, and for fixed-first include the fixed origin in the reachable union. (6) Fixed-first does not enforce minimum separation—joint mode rejects pairs below minimumOriginSeparation, but fixed-first mode does not; rankSecondOrigins only filters by object identity, not position or distance, so even an identical candidate position survives; add distance(first.position, candidate.position) >= minimumOriginSeparation. Important refinements: the 'four-level refinement' is not truly iterative—for every seed all offsets are generated around the original seed (seed ± spacing/2, ± spacing/4, ± spacing/8, ± spacing/16) without selecting the best half-step result and centering the quarter-step search around that new result; it is still a useful multiresolution neighborhood sample but not the coordinate/pattern refinement described in the plan. Local candidates can float between floors—candidate validation only checks whether a floor exists somewhere below the candidate, and local offsets retain the original Y coordinate, so on sloped terrain or multilevel sets an offset can move over a lower floor while preserving the upper floor's camera height, leaving the panorama origin floating several meters above the new floor; for each offset, find the floor under the new X/Z, set Y = floorY + panoramaHeightMeters, then perform clearance. The optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules—the optimizer evaluates angle and texel density, but when both panoramas are visible the actual shader still blends them only by distance, so the optimized coverage result and the visible result do not fully agree; the shader should use the same approximate quality function and preferably winner-takes-most selection rather than broad continuous averaging. Testing assessment: current tests are good unit tests but the most dangerous cases are absent: one large imported object containing an entire room, a 100k+ triangle performance fixture, reachableCoverage >= combinedCoverage invariant, fixed-first candidate separation, sloped and multilevel floors, existing panorama origins remaining immutable, and candidate generation inside concave imported geometry. There are no GitHub Actions workflow runs attached to the latest head, so the reported test suite has not been independently enforced in CI. Overall verdict: algorithm architecture for normal graybox sets 8/10, correctness of the two search modes 7.5/10, readiness for complex imported sets 4/10, overall promising but not merge-ready as production. The math/search design is mostly right; blockers are implementation scale and one dangerous workflow decision. After required changes (replace AABB clearance with actual geometry clearance, replace object-heavy triangle/BVH data with typed arrays and transferable buffers, move extraction into the worker, remove ability to relocate existing panorama references, recalculate reported metrics on one common sample bank, enforce separation in fixed-first mode, reproject local refinement candidates onto their floor), the optimizer would be a strong, credible feature. Currently it should work nicely on ordinary PanoRef primitive sets, but the exact scenario motivating this feature—a complex imported production set—is where the current implementation is most likely to fail. Subsequent work: rebase onto main and resolve the PR conflict; add an allowed-floor-region mechanism or at least robust imported-floor component filtering; run one real complex imported-set benchmark and add a full 100K+ optimizer integration test, not merely a BVH-construction test; set a goal to accomplish the above, and when work is complete, spawn a subagent whose job is to disprove that the goal is actually fully complete, have it report back what still is lacking, then fix that, and repeat that process until the subagent is unable to find any holes in the implementation. A patch was applied to remove the stale PROJECTED_FALLOFF = 6.0 constant and replace the assertion with one protecting the new optimizer-aligned angle/texel-quality selection and dominance modes (projectedQualityAt, projectedBlendMode == 2 ? 1.15 : 1.0, projectedBlendMode == 3 ? 1.15 : 1.0, and not projectedConfidence); the targeted regression test (multiOriginInteraction.test.ts) passed with 36 tests. Full test suite (42 test files, 371 tests) passed, lint (tsc --noEmit) passed, and build (vite build) passed. Notable test durations: projectionCoverage.test.ts (10 tests, 39235ms) runs both complete optimizer modes on a 100k+ triangle indexed fixture; occlusionPixel.test.ts (1 test, 3973ms) generates a valid depth cubemap via real WebGL pixel readback; projectedStyleCompile.test.ts (2 tests, 3934ms) compiles projected materials under real WebGL with single and dual projector modes; projectedReceive.test.ts (1 test, 4309ms) receives projected-style material via real WebGL pixel readback.
